goal: Add unit tests for the notifications module and the admin module, and document the exported types in the TypeScript client.

plan.goal: Add unit tests for notifications and admin modules and document the exported types in the TypeScript client.
plan.rationale: The notifications and admin modules currently lack direct unit test coverage, while the TypeScript client's exported types need clearer documentation. Adding focused pytest tests and JSDoc comments improves coverage and maintainability without changing runtime behavior.

tasks.title: Add unit tests for notifications module
tasks.instructions: Create tests/test_notifications.py with pytest unit tests covering all public functions and main paths in src/notifications.py. Use monkeypatch or unittest.mock to isolate external side effects and follow the existing test style used in tests/test_auth.py, tests/test_orders.py, and tests/test_users.py.

tasks.title: Add unit tests for admin module
tasks.instructions: Create tests/test_admin.py with pytest unit tests covering all public functions and main paths in src/admin.py. Use mocks or monkeypatch to isolate external dependencies and keep tests consistent with the existing test files.

tasks.title: Document exported types in TypeScript client
tasks.instructions: Add JSDoc comments to all exported types and interfaces in src/client/types.ts. Document the purpose, key properties, and any important usage notes. Do not change runtime behavior or type contracts.

results.notes: The model notes were not valid JSON. The committed diff is the result.

No files were changed in this run: the file-editing tool reported that it had already been invoked twice and refused further calls, so the diff is empty and the requested test module was not created. No manual edits were made, per the constraint that the editing tool is the only way files change. A fresh run with the editing tool available is required to add the pytest unit tests covering the target module's public functions and main paths with mocked external dependencies.

Added JSDoc comments to all six exported interfaces in src/client/types.ts: CreateOrderRequest, Order, ChargeRequest, ChargeResult, LoginRequest, and Session. Each block documents purpose via a summary line, key properties via @property tags, and usage notes via @remarks (e.g. token auth, HTTPS-only passwords, checking status before treating a charge as complete, supplying currency explicitly). Only comments were added — no runtime behavior, names, or type contracts were changed. git_diff confirms the change is limited to src/client/types.ts.
